facts.fact_text: Immediately after the announcement of the preliminary results of the 19 February 2008 presidential election, Mr Ter-Petrosyan called on his supporters to gather at Freedom Square in central Yerevan in order to protest against alleged irregularities in the election process.
From 20 February 2008 onwards, nationwide daily protest rallies were held by Mr Ter-Petrosyan's supporters.
The main meeting place of Mr Ter-Petrosyan's supporters during the protest rallies was Freedom Square and the surrounding park in Yerevan.
The rallies at Freedom Square attracted at times tens of thousands of people.
Several hundred demonstrators stayed in the Freedom Square area around the clock, having set up a camp.
On 22 February 2008 the applicant made a speech at the rally held at Freedom Square.
In his speech at Freedom Square on 22 February 2008, the applicant expressed his support for Mr Ter-Petrosyan.
In his speech at Freedom Square on 22 February 2008, the applicant criticised the conduct of the presidential election, alleging various types of irregularities.
In his speech at Freedom Square on 22 February 2008, the applicant called on those gathered not to give up and to stand by their votes.
In his speech at Freedom Square on 22 February 2008, the applicant said that rule of law had to be finally established in Armenia.
The applicant alleged that, following his speech at Freedom Square on 22 February 2008, the authorities started persecuting him and his family members.
On 22 February 2008, the same date as the applicant's speech at Freedom Square, the General Prosecutor applied to the President of Armenia seeking to have the applicant dismissed.
On 23 February 2008 the President of Armenia issued a decree dismissing the applicant from the post of Deputy General Prosecutor.
On 23 February 2008 the President of Armenia issued a decree depriving the applicant of his rank of First Category State Justice Councillor.
According to the applicant, the applicant, his brother V.J. and two others, together with their cars, were taken into police custody.

According to the record of bringing a person in, the applicant was brought in to the PDFOC on suspicion of illegal possession, carrying and transportation of arms and ammunition, and for showing resistance to police officers.

On 24 February 2008 at 1.10 a.m. a PDFOC investigator drew up a record of the applicant's arrest within the framework of the instituted criminal case, indicating 1.10 a.m. as the time of the applicant's arrest.

The record of the applicant's arrest stated that the applicant was arrested on suspicion of illegal acquisition, possession and carrying of arms and ammunition, as provided for by Article 235 § 1 of the Armenian Criminal Code.

Later on 24 February 2008 another criminal case was instituted under Article 235 § 1 of the Armenian Criminal Code (illegal acquisition, possession or carrying of arms and ammunition) in respect of the applicant.
On 26 February 2008 the applicant was formally charged under Article 235 § 1 of the Armenian Criminal Code (illegal acquisition, possession or carrying of arms and ammunition).
On 26 February 2008 the applicant was formally charged under Article 316 § 1 of the Armenian Criminal Code (non-life or health-threatening assault on a public official).
On 7 March 2008 the investigator decided to join the applicant's criminal case to case number 62202608.

The applicant submitted before the Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan that after arriving at the PDFOC he had been met by a large crowd of police officers who forcibly took him inside the building, and therefore the allegations of resistance or violence on his part were nonsense.

The Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan found on 19 June 2008 that, if the applicant remained at large, he could abscond, obstruct the proceedings by exerting pressure on the persons involved in the proceedings and, by his actions, hinder the further disclosure of the circumstances of the case.

In his appeal of 23 June 2008, the applicant argued that the Kentron and Nork-Marash District Court of Yerevan had failed to provide any reasons in support of its finding that he might abscond or obstruct the proceedings.

The Explanatory Memorandum to the Report on the Functioning of Democratic Institutions in Armenia (Doc. 11579) stated that those high-level state officials who publicly denounced the election were subsequently dismissed from their positions.

The Explanatory Memorandum to the Report on the Functioning of Democratic Institutions in Armenia (Doc. 11579) stated that a number of those high-level state officials, as well as several opposition activists, were arrested on seemingly artificial charges, which left the impression that their prosecution was politically motivated.
